title: Your own voice
job: An eight-sentence piece that changes register midway
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE PIVOT IS THE ONLY NEW THING. Every structure under it is owned: ammā … fa- is L4-M2's, ʿalā kulli ḥāl is L4-M4's, ʿalā ayy ḥāl is L4-M5's, fī an-nihāya is L1-M7's fī on L3-M10's nihāya. This rung spends two keys and re-uses the rest of the course.
M9 told one story twice. M10 turns ONCE, inside a single piece, and the turn is a change of REGISTER rather than of plot. L4-M10 owns the narrative twist and it is not repeated here.

English pivots register with a single word set down as its own sentence — Anyway. Right. So. Arabic's pivot is a CLAUSE. A bare ʿalā kulli ḥāl standing alone reads as an unfinished thought, not as a turn.

THE BEST PIECES HAVE A PIVOT SENTENCE THAT BELONGS TO BOTH HALVES. A piece that changes register between two paragraphs is two pieces stapled together; a piece that turns inside one sentence is one piece.

Nothing is taught here that is not the pivot. If a piece needs a key the ladder has not bought, the key belongs in an earlier module and the piece should be rewritten — there is no later module to defer it to. This is the only place in the course where that sentence is literally true.
The verb-before-subject law has been in force since L2-M10 and is deliberately not restated. At the last rung of the course you either have it or you do not.

The register moves in the GRAMMAR and not only in the words: wa becomes fa- and thumma, an active verb becomes yuqāl, and the clauses lengthen. Swapping nouns alone leaves the register exactly where it was — M9's rule, and the one this module is built on.
kadhālika carries the previous half forward; hākadhā sums it up; ʿalā kulli ḥāl steps back from it. Three different turns, and which one a piece takes decides what its second half is allowed to say.

sentences.display: ams, dhahabtu ilā as-sūq. kāna al-jaww bārid. iltaqaytu ṣadīqī hunāka. wa ishtaraytu al-khubz. kadhālika, kāna al-yawm ṭawīl. ammā as-sūq fa-kāna kabīr jiddan. yuqāl inna hādhā as-sūq qadīm. wa fī an-nihāya, kānat ar-riḥla mufīda.
sentences.script: أمس، ذهبت إلى السوق. كان الجو باردًا. التقيت صديقي هناك. واشتريت الخبز. كذلك، كان اليوم طويلًا. أما السوق فكان كبيرًا جدًا. يقال إن هذا السوق قديم. وفي النهاية، كانت الرحلة مفيدة.
sentences.cue: Yesterday I went to the market. The weather was cold. I met my friend there. And I bought the bread. Likewise, the day was long. As for the market, it was very large. It is said that this market is old. And in the end, the trip was a useful one.
sentences.literal: Yesterday, I-went to the-market. Was the-weather cold. I-met my-friend there. And I-bought the-bread. Likewise, was the-day long. As-for the-market so-was large very. It-is-said that this the-market old. And in the-end, was the-trip useful.

words.note: Likewise — the lightest of the three pivots. It carries the half just told forward into the next one instead of stepping back from it, and it opens its clause with a comma behind it.

sentences.trap: The turn is in the fifth sentence and it is easy to miss, because nothing in the vocabulary changes: wa gives way to ammā … fa-, an active verb gives way to yuqāl, and the clauses lengthen. That is the whole move.
sentences.sound: ka-DHĀ-li-ka stresses the long ā in the middle. Read the first four sentences quickly and the last three slower — the pace is part of the register.

variations.display: ams, dhahabtu ilā as-sūq. kāna al-jaww bārid. iltaqaytu ṣadīqī hunāka.
variations.script: أمس، ذهبت إلى السوق. كان الجو باردًا. التقيت صديقي هناك.
variations.cue: Yesterday I went to the market. The weather was cold. I met my friend there.
variations.changed: the plain half alone — no pivot, and so no second register

variations.display: kadhālika, kāna al-yawm ṭawīl. ammā as-sūq fa-kāna kabīr jiddan.
variations.script: كذلك، كان اليوم طويلًا. أما السوق فكان كبيرًا جدًا.
variations.cue: Likewise, the day was long. As for the market, it was very large.
variations.changed: the pivot and the sentence after it, which is where the register actually turns

mistake.display: ams, dhahabtu ilā as-sūq. kadhālika. kāna al-yawm ṭawīl.
mistake.script: أمس، ذهبت إلى السوق. كذلك. كان اليوم طويلًا.
mistake.why: kadhālika alone is not a sentence. English drops Likewise or Anyway in as a whole turn; Arabic's pivot is a clause, and the bare marker reads as a thought that stopped halfway.

sentences.usage: A day recounted to someone, then written down — a message that starts as talk and ends as a report.
sentences.mnemonic: Four quick, one turn, three long.

sentences.display: kāna hunāka qarār ṣaʿb. lam afham al-mushkila. qāla lī ṣadīqī: "lā aʿrif al-ḥall". wa kuntu mashghūl jiddan. kadhālika, kāna al-qarār muhimm. ammā al-ḥall fa-kāna sahl. min nāḥiya ad-dalīl qawī, wa min nāḥiya ukhrā al-iʿtirāḍ ḍaʿīf. khulāṣat al-qawl, kāna al-qarār ṣaḥīḥ.
sentences.script: كان هناك قرار صعب. لم أفهم المشكلة. قال لي صديقي: «لا أعرف الحل». وكنت مشغولًا جدًا. كذلك، كان القرار مهمًا. أما الحل فكان سهلًا. من ناحية الدليل قوي، ومن ناحية أخرى الاعتراض ضعيف. خلاصة القول، كان القرار صحيحًا.
sentences.cue: There was a difficult decision. I did not understand the problem. My friend said to me: "I do not know the solution." And I was very busy. Likewise, the decision was important. As for the solution, it was easy. On the one hand the evidence is strong, and on the other the objection is weak. The upshot is that the decision was right.
sentences.literal: Was there decision difficult. Not I-understood the-problem. Said to-me my-friend: "not I-know the-solution". And I-was busy very. Likewise, was the-decision important. As-for the-solution so-was easy. From side the-evidence strong, and from side other the-objection weak. Summary-of the-saying, was the-decision correct.

words.note: Likewise — the lightest of the three pivots. It carries the half just told forward into the next one instead of stepping back from it, and it opens its clause with a comma behind it.

sentences.trap: The second half is M6's argument machinery and the first half is L4-M10's plain account. Nothing between them is new — the piece is made entirely of rungs already climbed, which is what the last module is for.
sentences.sound: The quoted clause is said at the pace of speech and the last two sentences are not. khu-LĀ-ṣat al-QAWL is the slowest thing in the piece.

variations.display: kāna hunāka qarār ṣaʿb. lam afham al-mushkila. wa kuntu mashghūl jiddan.
variations.script: كان هناك قرار صعب. لم أفهم المشكلة. وكنت مشغولًا جدًا.
variations.cue: There was a difficult decision. I did not understand the problem. And I was very busy.
variations.changed: the plain half without the quotation, which is the lightest version of it

variations.display: kadhālika, kāna al-qarār muhimm. khulāṣat al-qawl, kāna al-qarār ṣaḥīḥ.
variations.script: كذلك، كان القرار مهمًا. خلاصة القول، كان القرار صحيحًا.
variations.cue: Likewise, the decision was important. The upshot is that the decision was right.
variations.changed: the pivot set directly against the close, with the argument taken out from between them

mistake.display: kāna hunāka qarār ṣaʿb. khulāṣat al-qawl, kāna al-qarār ṣaḥīḥ.
mistake.script: كان هناك قرار صعب. خلاصة القول، كان القرار صحيحًا.
mistake.why: A close with no pivot in front of it. khulāṣat al-qawl belongs to the formal half, and dropping it straight onto a plain sentence changes register without turning — which is the fault this whole module exists to prevent.

sentences.usage: A decision explained to a colleague and then justified in writing, in one piece.
sentences.mnemonic: The turn comes before the summary, never instead of it.

sentences.display: aḥkī lakum qiṣṣa ʿan ṣayyād. kāna yaskun qurb al-baḥr. dhahaba ilā al-baḥr kull yawm. wa wajada samak kathīr. hākadhā kānat al-ḥayāt hunāka. ammā aṣ-ṣayyād fa-kāna faqīr. yuqāl inna al-baṭal kāna saʿīd. wa fī an-nihāya, ʿāda an-nās jamīʿan ilā al-qarya.
sentences.script: أحكي لكم قصة عن صياد. كان يسكن قرب البحر. ذهب إلى البحر كل يوم. ووجد سمكًا كثيرًا. هكذا كانت الحياة هناك. أما الصياد فكان فقيرًا. يقال إن البطل كان سعيدًا. وفي النهاية، عاد الناس جميعًا إلى القرية.
sentences.cue: I am telling you a story about a fisherman. He used to live near the sea. He went to the sea every day. And he found a lot of fish. Such was life there. As for the fisherman, he was poor. It is said that the hero was happy. And in the end, the people all returned to the village.
sentences.literal: I-tell to-you-all story about fisherman. Was he-lives near the-sea. He-went to the-sea every day. And he-found fish much. Thus was the-life there. As-for the-fisherman so-was poor. It-is-said that the-hero was happy. And in the-end, returned the-people all to the-village.

words.note: Thus, in this way. It closes the plain half by summing it up in one clause, which is what lets the formal half read as a second look at the same events rather than as a second story.

sentences.trap: M9 would have told this story twice. M10 tells it once and turns in the middle, and the fifth sentence is doing both jobs — it ends the telling and opens the account.
sentences.sound: hā-ka-DHĀ leans on the long ā at the end. Said slowly it closes the half; said quickly it sounds like an aside.

variations.display: aḥkī lakum qiṣṣa ʿan ṣayyād. kāna yaskun qurb al-baḥr. wa wajada samak kathīr.
variations.script: أحكي لكم قصة عن صياد. كان يسكن قرب البحر. ووجد سمكًا كثيرًا.
variations.cue: I am telling you a story about a fisherman. He used to live near the sea. And he found a lot of fish.
variations.changed: the told half alone, which is M9's plain register untouched

variations.display: hākadhā kānat al-ḥayāt hunāka. ammā aṣ-ṣayyād fa-kāna faqīr.
variations.script: هكذا كانت الحياة هناك. أما الصياد فكان فقيرًا.
variations.cue: Such was life there. As for the fisherman, he was poor.
variations.changed: the pivot and the first formal sentence, which is the whole turn in two lines

mistake.display: aḥkī lakum qiṣṣa ʿan ṣayyād. ammā aṣ-ṣayyād fa-kāna faqīr. hākadhā kānat al-ḥayāt hunāka.
mistake.script: أحكي لكم قصة عن صياد. أما الصياد فكان فقيرًا. هكذا كانت الحياة هناك.
mistake.why: The pivot has been put after the turn instead of at it. hākadhā sums up what came before, so a formal sentence in front of it leaves the piece with two openings and no hinge.

sentences.usage: A told tale that ends as a written one — the shape of a story recounted and then set down.
sentences.mnemonic: hākadhā looks backwards; everything after it looks forwards.

sentences.display: ams, waṣaltu ilā al-maṭār. kānat ar-riḥla ṭawīla. raʾaytu ṣadīqī hunāka. wa dhahabnā ilā al-funduq. hākadhā kāna al-yawm. ammā al-funduq fa-kāna jamīl. yuqāl inna hādhā al-funduq qadīm. wa fī an-nihāya, kāna an-nawm sahl.
sentences.script: أمس، وصلت إلى المطار. كانت الرحلة طويلة. رأيت صديقي هناك. وذهبنا إلى الفندق. هكذا كان اليوم. أما الفندق فكان جميلًا. يقال إن هذا الفندق قديم. وفي النهاية، كان النوم سهلًا.
sentences.cue: Yesterday I arrived at the airport. The journey was long. I saw my friend there. And we went to the hotel. Such was the day. As for the hotel, it was beautiful. It is said that this hotel is old. And in the end, sleep came easily.
sentences.literal: Yesterday, I-arrived to the-airport. Was the-journey long. I-saw my-friend there. And we-went to the-hotel. Thus was the-day. As-for the-hotel so-was beautiful. It-is-said that this the-hotel old. And in the-end, was the-sleep easy.

words.note: Thus, in this way. It closes the plain half by summing it up in one clause, which is what lets the formal half read as a second look at the same events rather than as a second story.

sentences.trap: Count the connectors rather than the words: wa, wa, wa in the first half and ammā … fa-, yuqāl, wa fī an-nihāya in the second. The nouns are the same kind of nouns throughout, and the register has moved anyway.
sentences.sound: wa-ṢAL-tu lands on the heavy ṣ. The three formal sentences are longer in the mouth as well as on the page, and reading them at the pace of the first four flattens the piece.

variations.display: ams, waṣaltu ilā al-maṭār. kānat ar-riḥla ṭawīla. wa dhahabnā ilā al-funduq.
variations.script: أمس، وصلت إلى المطار. كانت الرحلة طويلة. وذهبنا إلى الفندق.
variations.cue: Yesterday I arrived at the airport. The journey was long. And we went to the hotel.
variations.changed: the plain half alone, strung on wa

variations.display: ammā al-funduq fa-kāna jamīl. wa fī an-nihāya, kāna an-nawm sahl.
variations.script: أما الفندق فكان جميلًا. وفي النهاية، كان النوم سهلًا.
variations.cue: As for the hotel, it was beautiful. And in the end, sleep came easily.
variations.changed: the formal half alone, with the pivot removed — it reads as the end of a different piece

mistake.display: ams, waṣaltu ilā al-maṭār. wa dhahabnā ilā al-funduq. wa kāna al-funduq jamīl. wa kāna an-nawm sahl.
mistake.script: أمس، وصلت إلى المطار. وذهبنا إلى الفندق. وكان الفندق جميلًا. وكان النوم سهلًا.
mistake.why: Every clause on wa and nothing else. This is the piece with its register switched off: the same facts, the same words, and no turn anywhere in it — which is what a learner produces when they change the nouns and leave the grammar alone.

sentences.usage: A trip described to a friend and then written up — a message, then a note for the record.
sentences.mnemonic: Watch the connectors, not the nouns.

sentences.display: kuntu adrus fī al-jāmiʿa. kāna at-taʿlīm ghālī. lākin al-ʿamal kāna ṣaʿb. wa lam afham kull shayʾ. ʿalā kulli ḥāl, kāna at-taʿlīm mufīd. ammā al-imtiḥān fa-kāna ṣaʿb. min nāḥiya at-taʿlīm ghālī, wa min nāḥiya ukhrā huwa mufīd. khulāṣat al-qawl, at-taʿlīm ahamm min al-māl.
sentences.script: كنت أدرس في الجامعة. كان التعليم غاليًا. لكن العمل كان صعبًا. ولم أفهم كل شيء. على كل حال، كان التعليم مفيدًا. أما الامتحان فكان صعبًا. من ناحية التعليم غالي، ومن ناحية أخرى هو مفيد. خلاصة القول، التعليم أهم من المال.
sentences.cue: I used to study at the university. Education was expensive. But the work was hard. And I did not understand everything. In any case, education was useful. As for the exam, it was hard. On the one hand education is expensive, and on the other it is useful. The upshot is that education is more important than money.
sentences.literal: I-was I-study in the-university. Was the-education expensive. But the-work was difficult. And not I-understood every thing. In-any case, was the-education useful. As-for the-exam so-was difficult. From side the-education expensive, and from side other he useful. Summary-of the-saying, the-education more-important than the-money.

words.note: L4-M4's step-back marker, pointed back at rather than re-taught: note the spelling, kulli with the i, and that L4-M5's ʿalā ayy ḥāl does the same work. M10 buys no third way of saying it.

sentences.trap: ʿalā kulli ḥāl steps BACK from what was said rather than carrying it forward, so the second half is free to disagree with the first. kadhālika would not have allowed that.
sentences.sound: ʿa-lā KUL-li ḤĀL doubles the l of kulli and closes on the tight throat-h. It is three words and one movement — do not pause inside it.

variations.display: kuntu adrus fī al-jāmiʿa. kāna at-taʿlīm ghālī. wa lam afham kull shayʾ.
variations.script: كنت أدرس في الجامعة. كان التعليم غاليًا. ولم أفهم كل شيء.
variations.cue: I used to study at the university. Education was expensive. And I did not understand everything.
variations.changed: the plain half alone, which reads as a complaint rather than as a case

variations.display: ʿalā kulli ḥāl, kāna at-taʿlīm mufīd. khulāṣat al-qawl, at-taʿlīm ahamm min al-māl.
variations.script: على كل حال، كان التعليم مفيدًا. خلاصة القول، التعليم أهم من المال.
variations.cue: In any case, education was useful. The upshot is that education is more important than money.
variations.changed: the pivot against the close, with the argument between them removed

mistake.display: kuntu adrus fī al-jāmiʿa. ʿalā kulli ḥāl. kāna at-taʿlīm mufīd.
mistake.script: كنت أدرس في الجامعة. على كل حال. كان التعليم مفيدًا.
mistake.why: ʿalā kulli ḥāl is not a sentence on its own. English sets Anyway down as a whole turn and Arabic does not: the marker needs the clause it is turning into, or it reads as a thought abandoned.

sentences.usage: An account of your own years that ends as an argument — a personal statement, or an answer to why it was worth it.
sentences.mnemonic: kadhālika carries on; ʿalā kulli ḥāl steps back.

sentences.display: lam afham hādhihi al-kalima. qultu: "mā maʿnā hādhihi al-kalima". qāla lī ṣadīqī: "hiya nawʿ min al-adawāt". wa fahimtu tamāman. kadhālika, kānat al-kalima sahla. ammā al-qāmūs fa-kāna mufīd. yuqāl inna hādhihi al-lugha ṣaʿba. wa fī an-nihāya, fahimtu al-farq.
sentences.script: لم أفهم هذه الكلمة. قلت: «ما معنى هذه الكلمة». قال لي صديقي: «هي نوع من الأدوات». وفهمت تمامًا. كذلك، كانت الكلمة سهلة. أما القاموس فكان مفيدًا. يقال إن هذه اللغة صعبة. وفي النهاية، فهمت الفرق.
sentences.cue: I did not understand this word. I said: "What does this word mean?" My friend said to me: "It is a kind of tool." And I understood completely. Likewise, the word was easy. As for the dictionary, it was useful. It is said that this language is difficult. And in the end, I understood the difference.
sentences.literal: Not I-understood this the-word. I-said: "what meaning-of this the-word". Said to-me my-friend: "she kind of the-tools". And I-understood completely. Likewise, was the-word easy. As-for the-dictionary so-was useful. It-is-said that this the-language difficult. And in the-end, I-understood the-difference.

words.note: Likewise — the lightest of the three pivots. It carries the half just told forward into the next one instead of stepping back from it, and it opens its clause with a comma behind it.

sentences.trap: The first half is M8's repair happening live and the second half is the same event reported afterwards. Reading the whole piece as one register is the mistake — the quotations belong to one half only.
sentences.sound: The two quoted clauses are said faster and higher than the sentences around them; that difference is the plain register, and it disappears entirely after the pivot.

variations.display: lam afham hādhihi al-kalima. qultu: "mā maʿnā hādhihi al-kalima".
variations.script: لم أفهم هذه الكلمة. قلت: «ما معنى هذه الكلمة».
variations.cue: I did not understand this word. I said: "What does this word mean?"
variations.changed: the repair alone, in the moment it happened

variations.display: kadhālika, kānat al-kalima sahla. wa fī an-nihāya, fahimtu al-farq.
variations.script: كذلك، كانت الكلمة سهلة. وفي النهاية، فهمت الفرق.
variations.cue: Likewise, the word was easy. And in the end, I understood the difference.
variations.changed: the pivot and the close, with the account between them removed

mistake.display: lam afham hādhihi al-kalima. wa fī an-nihāya, fahimtu al-farq.
mistake.script: لم أفهم هذه الكلمة. وفي النهاية، فهمت الفرق.
mistake.why: Two sentences, two registers, no pivot between them. The piece has jumped rather than turned, and a reader hears a missing middle rather than a change of voice.

sentences.usage: Telling someone how you got past a word you did not have, and then writing the same thing down for yourself.
sentences.mnemonic: Quotations belong to the half before the turn.

sentences.display: qultu inna hādhā al-qarār ṣaḥīḥ. lākin baʿḍ an-nās yaʿtariḍ. attafiq maʿa hādhihi al-ḥujja. wa lā afham al-iʿtirāḍ. ʿalā kulli ḥāl, al-ḥujja qawiyya. awwalan, ad-dalīl wāḍiḥ. thāniyan, qad yaqūl qāʾil inna al-waqt ṣaʿb, ghayr anna at-tajriba ahamm. bi-ikhtiṣār, al-iʿtirāḍ ḍaʿīf.
sentences.script: قلت إن هذا القرار صحيح. لكن بعض الناس يعترض. أتفق مع هذه الحجة. ولا أفهم الاعتراض. على كل حال، الحجة قوية. أولًا، الدليل واضح. ثانيًا، قد يقول قائل إن الوقت صعب، غير أن التجربة أهم. باختصار، الاعتراض ضعيف.
sentences.cue: I said that this decision is right. But some people object. I agree with this case. And I do not understand the objection. In any case, the case is strong. First, the evidence is clear. Second, someone may say that the time is short, except that the experience is more important. In short, the objection is weak.
sentences.literal: I-said that this the-decision correct. But some the-people objects. I-agree with this the-case. And not I-understand the-objection. In-any case, the-case strong. Firstly, the-evidence clear. Secondly, may says sayer that the-time difficult, other-than that the-experience more-important. In-brevity, the-objection weak.

words.note: L4-M4's step-back marker, pointed back at rather than re-taught: note the spelling, kulli with the i, and that L4-M5's ʿalā ayy ḥāl does the same work. M10 buys no third way of saying it.

sentences.trap: The pivot here turns an opinion into a case. Everything after it is M6's, and everything before it is ordinary talk — the piece is one argument that starts in a conversation and finishes in public.
sentences.sound: The first four sentences fall at the end; the numbered ones rise. AW-wa-lan and THĀ-ni-yan both clip their -an endings and both take a real pause after the comma.

variations.display: qultu inna hādhā al-qarār ṣaḥīḥ. lākin baʿḍ an-nās yaʿtariḍ.
variations.script: قلت إن هذا القرار صحيح. لكن بعض الناس يعترض.
variations.cue: I said that this decision is right. But some people object.
variations.changed: the opinion alone, before it becomes a case

variations.display: ʿalā kulli ḥāl, al-ḥujja qawiyya. bi-ikhtiṣār, al-iʿtirāḍ ḍaʿīf.
variations.script: على كل حال، الحجة قوية. باختصار، الاعتراض ضعيف.
variations.cue: In any case, the case is strong. In short, the objection is weak.
variations.changed: the pivot against the close, with the numbered case taken out

mistake.display: qultu inna hādhā al-qarār ṣaḥīḥ. awwalan, ad-dalīl wāḍiḥ. thāniyan, al-iʿtirāḍ ḍaʿīf.
mistake.script: قلت إن هذا القرار صحيح. أولًا، الدليل واضح. ثانيًا، الاعتراض ضعيف.
mistake.why: The numbered ladder has been started with no pivot in front of it. M6's markers belong to the formal half, and beginning them straight after a plain opinion makes the piece read as two documents rather than one turn.

sentences.usage: Defending a position that started as a remark — a thread, a meeting, an answer that grew.
sentences.mnemonic: The pivot is where an opinion becomes an argument.

sentences.display: ams, iltaqaytu jārī fī ash-shāriʿ. qāla lī: "anā mashghūl al-yawm". kāna mutaʿab jiddan. wa dhahabnā ilā al-maṭʿam. hākadhā badaʾa al-yawm. ammā al-maṭʿam fa-kāna jamīl. yuqāl inna hādhā al-maṭʿam qadīm. wa fī an-nihāya, ʿudtu ilā al-bayt.
sentences.script: أمس، التقيت جاري في الشارع. قال لي: «أنا مشغول اليوم». كان متعبًا جدًا. وذهبنا إلى المطعم. هكذا بدأ اليوم. أما المطعم فكان جميلًا. يقال إن هذا المطعم قديم. وفي النهاية، عدت إلى البيت.
sentences.cue: Yesterday I met my neighbour in the street. He said to me: "I am busy today." He was very tired. And we went to the restaurant. Thus the day began. As for the restaurant, it was beautiful. It is said that this restaurant is old. And in the end, I returned home.
sentences.literal: Yesterday, I-met my-neighbour in the-street. He-said to-me: "I busy the-day". Was tired very. And we-went to the-restaurant. Thus began the-day. As-for the-restaurant so-was beautiful. It-is-said that this the-restaurant old. And in the-end, I-returned to the-house.

words.note: Thus, in this way. It closes the plain half by summing it up in one clause, which is what lets the formal half read as a second look at the same events rather than as a second story.

sentences.trap: hākadhā badaʾa al-yawm belongs to both halves: it closes the meeting in the street and it opens the account of the day. A pivot that belongs to only one half leaves the piece in two.
sentences.sound: The quoted line is the fastest thing in the piece and hā-ka-DHĀ is the slowest. That contrast is the turn, and it is audible before any of the grammar is.

variations.display: ams, iltaqaytu jārī fī ash-shāriʿ. qāla lī: "anā mashghūl al-yawm".
variations.script: أمس، التقيت جاري في الشارع. قال لي: «أنا مشغول اليوم».
variations.cue: Yesterday I met my neighbour in the street. He said to me: "I am busy today."
variations.changed: the meeting alone, with its quotation — L4-M10's frame untouched

variations.display: hākadhā badaʾa al-yawm. wa fī an-nihāya, ʿudtu ilā al-bayt.
variations.script: هكذا بدأ اليوم. وفي النهاية، عدت إلى البيت.
variations.cue: Thus the day began. And in the end, I returned home.
variations.changed: the pivot against the close — the day's two ends with nothing between them

mistake.display: ams, iltaqaytu jārī fī ash-shāriʿ. hākadhā badaʾa al-yawm. qāla lī: "anā mashghūl al-yawm".
mistake.script: أمس، التقيت جاري في الشارع. هكذا بدأ اليوم. قال لي: «أنا مشغول اليوم».
mistake.why: The quotation has been left on the far side of the pivot. Direct speech belongs to the plain half; after the turn it has to be reported, not quoted, or the register snaps back.

sentences.usage: A day told to one person and summarised for another — the same events, twice, in one message.
sentences.mnemonic: The pivot sentence ends one half and starts the other.

sentences.display: al-yawm, al-jaww ḥārr jiddan. lā adhhab ilā al-ʿamal. kāna al-jaww bārid ams. wa lākin al-yawm ṭawīl. kadhālika, kāna as-safar ṣaʿb. ammā al-qiṭār fa-kāna mutaʾakhkhir. natījatan, waṣaltu mutaʾakhkhiran. bi-ikhtiṣār, kāna al-yawm ṣaʿb.
sentences.script: اليوم، الجو حار جدًا. لا أذهب إلى العمل. كان الجو باردًا أمس. ولكن اليوم طويل. كذلك، كان السفر صعبًا. أما القطار فكان متأخرًا. نتيجةً، وصلت متأخرًا. باختصار، كان اليوم صعبًا.
sentences.cue: Today the weather is very hot. I am not going to work. The weather was cold yesterday. But the day is long. Likewise, the travelling was hard. As for the train, it was late. As a result, I arrived late. In short, the day was hard.
sentences.literal: The-day, the-weather hot very. Not I-go to the-work. Was the-weather cold yesterday. And but the-day long. Likewise, was the-travel difficult. As-for the-train so-was late. As-a-result, I-arrived late. In-brevity, was the-day difficult.

words.note: Likewise — the lightest of the three pivots. It carries the half just told forward into the next one instead of stepping back from it, and it opens its clause with a comma behind it.

sentences.trap: The first sentence is M7's indirect complaint — al-jaww ḥārr said in a room — and the last is M6's close. The piece walks the whole level in eight sentences and buys nothing to do it.
sentences.sound: na-tī-JA-tan clips its ending like awwalan and thālithan do. The first half can be muttered; the second cannot.

variations.display: al-yawm, al-jaww ḥārr jiddan. lā adhhab ilā al-ʿamal.
variations.script: اليوم، الجو حار جدًا. لا أذهب إلى العمل.
variations.cue: Today the weather is very hot. I am not going to work.
variations.changed: the complaint alone, which M7 would leave exactly here

variations.display: ammā al-qiṭār fa-kāna mutaʾakhkhir. natījatan, waṣaltu mutaʾakhkhiran.
variations.script: أما القطار فكان متأخرًا. نتيجةً، وصلت متأخرًا.
variations.cue: As for the train, it was late. As a result, I arrived late.
variations.changed: the formal half alone, which is L4-M2's cause and effect doing the work

mistake.display: al-yawm, al-jaww ḥārr jiddan. natījatan, waṣaltu mutaʾakhkhiran.
mistake.script: اليوم، الجو حار جدًا. نتيجةً، وصلت متأخرًا.
mistake.why: natījatan needs a cause in front of it, and a pivot before that. Dropped straight onto the complaint it claims a connection the piece has not made, and the register jumps at the same time.

sentences.usage: A day complained about and then explained — the message you send in the morning and the one you send at night.
sentences.mnemonic: Complaint first, account second, pivot between.

sentences.display: badaʾtu hādhihi al-lugha qabla sana. kānat kull kalima ṣaʿba. lam afham al-lahja. wa kuntu adrus kull yawm. ʿalā kulli ḥāl, al-ān aḥkī qiṣṣa bi-al-ʿarabiyya. ammā al-yawm al-awwal fa-kāna ṣaʿb. yuqāl inna hādhihi al-lugha ṣaʿba, ghayr anna at-tajriba ahamm. khulāṣat al-qawl, kānat at-tajriba mumtāza.
sentences.script: بدأت هذه اللغة قبل سنة. كانت كل كلمة صعبة. لم أفهم اللهجة. وكنت أدرس كل يوم. على كل حال، الآن أحكي قصة بالعربية. أما اليوم الأول فكان صعبًا. يقال إن هذه اللغة صعبة، غير أن التجربة أهم. خلاصة القول، كانت التجربة ممتازة.
sentences.cue: I began this language a year ago. Every word was difficult. I did not understand the dialect. And I used to study every day. In any case, now I tell a story in Arabic. As for the first day, it was hard. It is said that this language is difficult, except that the experience is more important. The upshot is that the experience was excellent.
sentences.literal: I-began this the-language before year. Was every word difficult. Not I-understood the-dialect. And I-was I-study every day. In-any case, the-now I-tell story in-the-Arabic. As-for the-day the-first so-was difficult. It-is-said that this the-language difficult, other-than that the-experience more-important. Summary-of the-saying, was the-experience excellent.

words.note: L4-M4's step-back marker, pointed back at rather than re-taught: note the spelling, kulli with the i, and that L4-M5's ʿalā ayy ḥāl does the same work. M10 buys no third way of saying it.

sentences.trap: This is the last piece of the last rung, and the honest test of it is that nothing in it is new. If a word here surprises you, it was bought earlier in the course and the surprise is the point.
sentences.sound: The pivot sentence is the only one in the piece that is in the present, and it should be said as though the sentence before it were still hanging in the air.

variations.display: badaʾtu hādhihi al-lugha qabla sana. kānat kull kalima ṣaʿba.
variations.script: بدأت هذه اللغة قبل سنة. كانت كل كلمة صعبة.
variations.cue: I began this language a year ago. Every word was difficult.
variations.changed: the plain half alone — a memory, with nothing drawn from it

variations.display: ʿalā kulli ḥāl, al-ān aḥkī qiṣṣa bi-al-ʿarabiyya.
variations.script: على كل حال، الآن أحكي قصة بالعربية.
variations.cue: In any case, now I tell a story in Arabic.
variations.changed: the pivot on its own, which is the only sentence of the piece that belongs to both halves

mistake.display: badaʾtu hādhihi al-lugha qabla sana. ammā al-yawm al-awwal fa-kāna ṣaʿb. ʿalā kulli ḥāl, al-ān aḥkī qiṣṣa bi-al-ʿarabiyya.
mistake.script: بدأت هذه اللغة قبل سنة. أما اليوم الأول فكان صعبًا. على كل حال، الآن أحكي قصة بالعربية.
mistake.why: The pivot has been put after the formal half instead of at the hinge. A piece can only turn once, and turning at the end leaves the reader with a conclusion and then a fresh start.

sentences.usage: The last thing you write in a language before you stop calling yourself a learner.
sentences.mnemonic: Nothing new — and that is the whole exam.

comprehensionPool.display: ams, dhahabtu ilā as-sūq. kadhālika, kāna al-yawm ṭawīl.
comprehensionPool.script: أمس، ذهبت إلى السوق. كذلك، كان اليوم طويلًا.
comprehensionPool.cue: Yesterday I went to the market. Likewise, the day was long.
As for the market, it was very large.

comprehensionPool.script: على كل حال، كان التعليم مفيدًا.
comprehensionPool.cue: In any case, education was useful.
It is said that this hotel is old.

comprehensionPool.cue: And in the end, I returned home.
In any case, the case is strong.
As a result, I arrived late.
